references.text: Earlier in the chapter, the provision for someone who is poor and cannot afford the usual cleansing offering is described, as verse 32 summarizes.
The introduction to the entire law concerning cleansing from leprosy, which verse 32 gives a concluding summary of.
Describes the diagnosis of leprosy (צָרַעַת), which is the condition addressed by the cleansing law in chapter 14.
Another example of adapting sacrifice requirements for the poor who cannot afford it (לֹא תַשִּׂיג יָדוֹ).
Further provision regarding an alternative offering for those who cannot afford it, following the same principle as in 14:32.
Parallel provision for a reduced offering for someone who cannot afford it, concerning cleansing after childbirth.
Jesus heals a leper and commands him to show himself to the priest and offer a sacrifice as Moses prescribed, referring to Leviticus 14.
